_comment: What every page in the menu reads as it opens, and how many requests
that takes: rule 8 in CLAUDE.md (2 Oct), so a module added to the app
cannot quietly slow the pages already there. reads_suite opens each page
as the admin on one small seeded house with the menu's counts switched
off, and fails a node that is neither on the page's line nor the
shell's, and a page whose own requests grew past its max; then it
measures the counts on one page against 'counts'.
A new page in the menu needs its line here, and the suite fails until it
has one. A module's count is its node in 'counts' and its requests in
that max - one small request is the rule. Another module's node turning
up on a page's line is the thing to stop and ask about: the lines below
were recorded as the app stood on 2 Oct, and the cross-module reads on
them were each put there on purpose, the Dashboard's above all (rule 7,
dashboard_sources.json). A node is the first part of the path:
/bookings/b1/prearrival is bookings. Rewrite a line from

shell._comment: Read by every page: the login (staff, permissions) and the menu's own announcement (menu).

counts._comment: The menu's counts as the admin sees them on Reservations: Spa's (spa and every booking), Chat's (contactnew, asked shallow), Tasks' (contactsettings, then one query per team - six). Asked once as a page opens since 2 Oct, and again on their own timers.
